title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Euler treats the transverse vibrations of an elastic rod EF of length a with equation (1/2g) y_tt = -b c^2 y_ssss. Regular (normal-mode) motions have the form y = C sin(ζ + t·ω²c√(2gb)/a²)·(α e^{uω} + β e^{-uω} + γ sin uω + δ cos uω), with u = s/a. In the case under study the rod is pinned ('stylo simpliciter fixa') at both ends E and F. It is also pinned at the midpoint L, but continuous through L. Matching the two portions EL and LF at L, with zero deflection there and continuity of slope and moment, gives a frequency determinant that factors into two pieces.

First factor (end of §50, this page), sin ½ω = 0, i.e. ω = 2iπ.
- Euler's general coefficient formulas from the previous page have the vanishing factor sin ½ω in their denominators. He multiplies them all through by it.
- In the limit α = β = δ = 0 and α' = β' = δ' = 0. Also γ = -(1-e^ω)(e^ω-1) = (e^ω-1)², and γ' = (e^ω-1)(1-e^ω) = -γ, using cos ω = 1.
- Normalising γ = 1, γ' = -1, the mode is y = ±C sin(...)·sin(uω).
- Each half is a simply-supported sine wave of length a/2. These are the antisymmetric modes of the two-span continuous beam, and they coincide with case IV (pinned–pinned) at half length: frequencies ×4, i.e. two octaves higher.

Second factor (§51), tan ½ω = (e^ω-1)/(e^ω+1) = tanh ½ω.
- This is the case V (pinned–clamped) frequency equation with ω replaced by ½ω, again because each portion has length a/2.
- Euler concludes that each half vibrates as if pinned at E (or F) and rigidly clamped at L. These are the symmetric modes, in which the slope at the middle support vanishes by symmetry.
- He gives ω ≈ 5π/2, 9π/2, 13π/2, ..., i.e. ½ω ≈ (4k+1)π/4, the tanh≈1 approximation. Sounds are again two octaves above case V.
- He stresses as 'maxime notatu dignum' that the two halves can vibrate in two distinct manners, one matching case IV and one matching case V.
errors: The ω values 5π/2, 9π/2, ... for the second family are only asymptotic approximations obtained by setting tanh ½ω = 1. The exact first root is ½ω = 3.92660 versus 5π/4 = 3.92699, so ω ≈ 7.8532, not 7.8540. The error is tiny and decreases rapidly, but Euler states the values without qualification.

Sign/convention point: the true antisymmetric mode of the continuous rod is sin(2iπ s/a) over the whole length, with continuous slope at L. Euler writes y = -C sin(uω) on LF with 'u = s/a'. This is correct only if the abscissa on LF is measured from F, since sin(2iπ(1-u)) = -sin(2iπu). If s is measured from E throughout, the minus sign would produce a slope discontinuity at L. The page does not make the convention explicit, so the formula as written is ambiguous.

The previous page's list of frequencies (transcribed '4π c√2gb/aa, 16π..., 36π...') should involve π², since ω = 2iπ gives ω² = 4i²π². This is likely a transcription or print slip, consistent with the ω²c√(2gb)/a² formula on this page.

Deriving the mode shape by multiplying the general coefficient formulas through by the vanishing factor sin ½ω is a delicate limiting procedure. It happens to give a consistent ratio γ' = -γ (cos ω = 1 at the roots), but Euler does not justify it.

ideas.what: Frequency determinant of a two-span continuous beam (pinned ends, intermediate pinned support at midpoint) factors into antisymmetric and symmetric families
ideas.modern_name: Symmetric/antisymmetric mode decomposition of a two-span continuous Euler–Bernoulli beam
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E526) as part of his catalogue of rod boundary conditions; later standard in Rayleigh's Theory of Sound and in engineering texts
ideas.where_published: E526 itself (Acta Acad. Sci. Petrop. 1779 [1782]); discussed in Truesdell's 1960 account of the rational mechanics of elastic bodies (Opera omnia II.11 part 2)

ideas.what: Antisymmetric modes: each half behaves as a pinned–pinned beam of length a/2, so the frequencies are 4 times (two octaves above) those of the full pinned–pinned rod
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (1744 onward; Daniel Bernoulli also had the L^-2 law)

ideas.what: Symmetric modes: each half behaves as a pinned–clamped beam, with frequency equation tan(ω/2) = tanh(ω/2)
ideas.modern_name: Clamped–pinned beam frequency equation tan βL = tanh βL, applied by symmetry
ideas.where_published: E526 case V and this section

ideas.what: Asymptotic roots ω ≈ (4k+1)π/2, obtained by replacing tanh with 1
ideas.modern_name: Asymptotic eigenvalues of the clamped–pinned beam

deep.surprise_reason: The page completes a standard, well-documented case of E526 (an intermediate support splitting the rod into two halves vibrating in two ways). The physics and mathematics are correct apart from approximate roots and an unspecified sign convention. Truesdell's history of elastic rods covers E526's catalogue of cases, so nothing here appears absent from the literature.
